topics.title: Design a Web Crawler
topics.description: Understanding large-scale web crawling systems including URL frontier management, politeness, duplicate detection, and performance optimization.

subtopics.title: Web Crawler
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Web Crawler

Interview Definition

A web crawler (also called a spider or bot) is a distributed system that automatically discovers, downloads, and processes web content by traversing hyperlinks starting from seed URLs.



Important Points

Web = Directed graph (pages = nodes, links = edges)

Uses BFS-based traversal

Must support scalability

Must enforce politeness

Must handle duplicates & failures



Advantages

Enables search engines

Supports web archiving

Enables data mining

Supports monitoring & analytics



Disadvantages

Heavy bandwidth usage

Can overload websites

Complex at scale

Difficult freshness management



Basic Flow

Start with seed URLs

Add to URL Frontier

Download page

Parse content

Extract new URLs

Store content

Repeat



Important Word Definitions

Directed Graph – A graph where edges have direction (web links).
Seed URL – Initial starting URL for crawling.
Crawl Budget – Maximum resources allocated for crawling.

subtopics.title: DFS vs BFS
subtopics.theory:
2️⃣ DFS vs BFS

Interview Definition

DFS explores depth-first, while BFS explores level-by-level. Web crawlers use BFS.



Important Points

DFS → Deep traversal

BFS → Level traversal using FIFO queue

BFS gives better coverage

BFS avoids deep trap risks



Advantages of BFS

Better page discovery

Controlled traversal

Easier prioritization



Disadvantages of DFS

Risk of infinite depth

Poor coverage early



Flow (BFS)

Enqueue seed

Dequeue URL

Extract links

Enqueue new URLs



Important Terms

FIFO – First In First Out queue.
Traversal – Visiting nodes in a graph.

subtopics.title: URL Frontier
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ URL Frontier ⭐ (Most Important)

Interview Definition

URL Frontier is a scheduling system that stores and manages URLs to be crawled while enforcing politeness, priority, and freshness.



Important Points

Splits crawl state:

To-be-downloaded

Already downloaded

Uses:

Front queues (priority)

Back queues (politeness)



Advantages

Prevents host overload

Enables priority crawling

Supports recrawling strategy



Disadvantages

Complex to implement

Requires disk + memory hybrid storage



Flow

URL arrives

Assign priority

Route to host queue

Worker downloads



Important Terms

Front Queue – Priority-based queue.
Back Queue – Host-based queue.
Politeness – Controlled request rate per host.
Freshness – Keeping content up-to-date.

subtopics.title: Politeness
subtopics.theory:
4️⃣ Politeness

Interview Definition

Politeness ensures the crawler does not send too many requests to the same host within a short period.



Important Points

One host → one active worker

Delay between requests

Respect robots.txt



Advantages

Avoid IP bans

Ethical crawling

Sustainable system



Disadvantages

Slower per-host crawl speed



Flow

Identify host

Enforce delay

Download page



Important Terms

Host – Domain server (example.com).
DOS Attack – Overloading a server with requests.

subtopics.title: Robots.txt
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Robots.txt

Interview Definition

Robots.txt is a file that specifies which URLs crawlers are allowed or disallowed to access.



Important Points

Located at: /robots.txt

Parsed before crawling

Cached per host



Advantages

Legal compliance

Respect website rules



Disadvantages

Not strictly enforceable

May be outdated



Flow

Fetch robots.txt

Parse rules

Cache rules

Allow or block crawling



Important Terms

User-agent – Identifier of crawler.
Disallow – Blocked path rule.

subtopics.title: HTML Downloader
subtopics.theory:
6️⃣ HTML Downloader

Interview Definition

HTML Downloader fetches web pages via HTTP/HTTPS using distributed workers.



Important Points

Multi-threaded

Distributed

Handles timeouts & retries

Uses DNS resolver



Advantages

High throughput

Parallel downloads



Disadvantages

Network bottleneck

DNS latency



Flow

Resolve DNS

Send HTTP request

Receive response

Pass to parser



Important Terms

DNS Resolver – Converts domain to IP.
Timeout – Maximum wait time.

subtopics.title: Duplicate Content Detection
subtopics.theory:
7️⃣ Duplicate Content Detection

Interview Definition

Duplicate detection identifies and removes identical web pages using content hashing.



Important Points

~30% web is duplicate

Use hash (MD5/SHA)

Store hash in “Content Seen?”



Advantages

Saves storage

Improves crawl efficiency

Better indexing quality



Disadvantages

Hash collisions possible (rare)

Near-duplicate detection complex



Flow

Normalize content

Generate hash

Check hash store

Store if new



Important Terms

Hash – Fixed-length fingerprint of data.
Collision – Two inputs producing same hash.

subtopics.title: Spider Traps
subtopics.theory:
8️⃣ Spider Traps

Interview Definition

Spider traps are infinite URL patterns that cause crawlers to enter endless loops.



Important Points

Infinite directory paths

Calendar traps

Parameter explosion



Advantages of Detection

Saves crawl budget

Prevents infinite loops



Disadvantages

Hard to detect automatically



Prevention Flow

Detect abnormal growth

Apply URL length limits

Enforce crawl budget per site



Important Terms

Heuristic – Rule-based detection approach.
Crawl Budget – Max pages per domain.

subtopics.title: Data Noise Filtering
subtopics.theory:
9️⃣ Data Noise Filtering

Interview Definition

Data noise filtering removes low-value or spam content during crawling.



Important Points

URL filtering

Content-based filtering

Spam detection



Advantages

Better data quality

Efficient storage use



Disadvantages

Risk of filtering useful pages



Flow

Pre-filter URL

Download

Content quality check

Store or discard



Important Terms

Spam – Low-quality or manipulative content.
Boilerplate – Repeated template content.

subtopics.title: Performance Optimization
subtopics.theory:
🔟 Performance Optimization

Interview Definition

Performance optimization improves crawl throughput while respecting system constraints.



Important Points

Distributed crawling

DNS caching

Geographic locality

Short timeouts



Advantages

High scalability

Efficient bandwidth use



Disadvantages

Increased system complexity



Important Terms

Geographic Locality – Deploying servers near target regions.
Persistent Connection – Reusing TCP connection.

subtopics.title: Robustness
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣1️⃣ Robustness

Interview Definition

Robustness ensures crawler reliability despite failures.



Important Points

Save crawl state

Retry policies

Exception handling

Consistent hashing



Advantages

Fault tolerance

Resume after crash



Disadvantages

Extra storage overhead



Important Terms

Consistent Hashing – Distributes data across nodes with minimal reshuffling.
Fault Tolerance – Ability to survive failures.

subtopics.title: Extensibility
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣2️⃣ Extensibility

Interview Definition

Extensibility allows new modules and content types to be added without redesigning the system.



Important Points

Modular architecture

Plug-in design

Loose coupling



Advantages

Future-proof design

Easy upgrades



Disadvantages

Over-engineering risk



Important Terms

Loose Coupling – Components operate independently.
Plug-in Module – Add-on component.

subtopics.title: Final Interview Summary
subtopics.theory:
✅ Final Interview Summary

A web crawler is a distributed BFS-based system that uses a URL frontier to enforce politeness, prioritization, and freshness while handling duplicates, spider traps, noise, and failures at web scale.
